subject: PayGrid model-fit evals / parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir.k@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks for taking the time today — good discussion on PayGrid's fraud-detection assistant use case and the performance requirements for transaction triage. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goals: match PayGrid's existing proprietary baseline on critical accuracy slice (transaction-level fraud classification + explanation coherence) while improving latency/cost by ~20% on batch scoring.
- Redwood recommendation (initial eval set): Llama-2-70B-Chat (quantized 8-bit) and Mistral-Instruct-7B as the open-model candidates; we'll also run our tuned production variant for comparison so you can see delta vs your baseline.
- Deliverables from Redwood: evaluation harness, prompt set (attached), example inference configs, and a rubric for parity thresholds.
- Action items:
  1) I attached paygrid_prompt_set_v2.txt and paygrid_eval_template.xlsx — please confirm these prompts represent your most common user flows (triage, explainability snippets).
  2) We'll run a 10k-sample eval (paygrid-provided) and share benchmark PDF + raw CSV within 5 business days after you confirm sample availability.
  3) You mentioned an internal parity threshold — can you confirm if you want strict metric parity (>=99% of key metric) or a softer acceptance band (<=2% relative drop) for the pilot?

If that matches your expectations I can kick off the eval and loop in Marissa on commercial/packaging if we need dedicated capacity.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: paygrid_prompt_set_v2.txt
Attachment: paygrid_eval_template.xlsx
From: Samir Khanna <samir.k@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gutiérrez <elena.g@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Thanks Lauren — this is very clear and close to what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Parity: our internal bar for the pilot is fairly high because the current model is safety-critical in edge cases. We want:
  * Precision on the high-risk fraud class >= 98.5% (relative to our baseline)
  * No more than 1.5% degradation in explainability score on the manual review set

If an open model meets these, we can move to a 30k-sample extended eval. If not, we'll need a short gap analysis.

- Data: we can share the 10k sample by EOD tomorrow; it's redacted but includes the necessary labels and reviewer notes.

One ask: could you include per-slice breakdowns (by transaction type and currency) in the report? Our coverage varies a lot by region.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khanna
Head of ML Ops, PayGrid
samir.k@paygrid.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir.k@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Appreciate the clarity, Samir. That parity spec is helpful — we'll treat the thresholds you listed as the acceptance criteria for the pilot run. A few notes on how we'll structure the evaluation: 

- Metrics: we'll report precision/recall/F1 for the high-risk class, explanation coherence scored against your reviewer labels (same rubric), and per-slice breakdowns (transaction type, currency, merchant vertical).
- Parity policy: we'll mark a model as "parity" if it meets both: (a) >=98.5% precision relative to your baseline and (b) <=1.5% degradation in explainability on the review set. If it misses one metric but is within 2% overall, we'll include a remediation plan and parameter tuning suggestions.
- Models to benchmark: Llama-2-70B-Chat (q8), Mistral-Instruct-7B (default), and Redwood-serving tuned variant (internal label: Redwood-Prod-v1) for a controlled comparison. For transparency we'll include raw logits and per-example deltas so you can reproduce.
- Timeline: once we receive the 10k sample, ETA for initial report is 5 business days. Extended 30k eval will be estimated after the initial pass.

Links: full benchmark methodology + eval harness here — https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/paygrid (we'll push a branch with your dataset). Also uploading a short PDF with benchmark definitions to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-paygrid-benchmarks

I'll start the run as soon as the sample lands. Marissa — can you confirm whether we should offer a discounted pilot bundle or include Dedicated credits if they want throughput guarantees? Aditya — can you stand by for any infra questions if we need to spin up extra capacity?

Thanks,
Lauren
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Looping in pricing/ops — quick notes:

- For a pilot (10k -> 5-day run + report) we have a standard pilot package: free eval credits up to $2k and a one-time professional services hour cap for analysis. If PayGrid wants guaranteed burst/throughput during evaluation or wants us to mirror production, we can propose a 3-month Dedicated trial with a reduced first-quarter commit.
- If they require SOC 2 evidence or network isolation for the sample transfer, we should confirm with Security. Samir, are you transferring via SFTP or an encrypted Drive link?

I'll prepare a short commercial one-pager and a draft SOW; Lauren, can you include the sections on acceptance criteria so the SOW references the parity thresholds?

-Marissa
From: Samir Khanna <samir.k@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gutiérrez <elena.g@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Lauren/Marissa —

We uploaded the 10k redacted sample to the Drive folder (link shared via SFTP token) and confirmed SOC 2 export controls with our security team — SFTP is preferred. Please proceed with the run.

Also, we reviewed the parity policy you proposed and are comfortable with the pilot acceptance criteria (>=98.5% precision; <=1.5% explainability degradation). If an open model meets parity we will request the extended 30k eval and discuss a Dedicated trial.

Proposed check-in: can we get the initial report by next Tuesday (2026-03-10)?

Thanks,
Samir
